text: the .gitattributes line is the only artifact cairn init writes without a cairns marker, so in a repo that already had one it is indistinguishable from a rule the user wrote themselves

author: agent
text: mark the .gitattributes rule with '# cairns:attributes' because an unmarked merge=union line is indistinguishable from a rule the user wrote themselves, so removal had no safe way to tell them apart

author: agent
text: uninstall keeps .tasks/ unless --purge because the board is the accumulated memory and the hooks are only plumbing — losing the record to a plumbing removal is the one unrecoverable outcome

author: agent
text: a hook without the cairns marker is reported as 'foreign' and left in place, since silently deleting someone else's hook is worse than leaving a stale one

author: agent
text: cairn init is now fully reversible. Every file it writes carries a marker (cairns:begin/end in CLAUDE.md, cairns:hook in .git/hooks, cairns:attributes in .gitattributes) and `cairn uninstall` strips exactly those, restoring a chained hook from its .pre-cairns backup and declining to touch any hook without the marker. .tasks/ survives unless --purge. Verified by round-trip in a real repo that already had a CLAUDE.md, a .gitattributes rule and a foreign post-commit hook — all three came back byte-identical.
